This Appeal Is Coming On For Hearing, This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mrs Justice P Sree Sudha
 Oral Judgment
Heard the arguments of both sides.
2. This appeal is filed against the judgment and award dated 06.01.2021 passed by the IV Additional Senior Civil Judge and Member, MACT - XV in MVC No.1551/2015.

3. The facts of the case are that, on 10.06.2015 at about 9:00 p.m., when the deceased, Baburaya,
was riding a motorcycle bearing registration No. MH-13/BK-7151 from Nandral to Bhatagunki village in a slow and cautious manner, a tractor bearing registration No. KA-28/TA-3047 came from the opposite direction at high speed, collided with the motorcycle, NC: 2025:KHC-K:5899 HC-KAR and caused the accident.
Baburaya, sustained severe injuries and died on the way to the hospital.
4. The claim petition was filed by the wife and parents of the deceased, seeking compensation of Rs.38,10,000 along with interest.
However, the Tribunal, after considering the entire material on record, granted compensation of Rs.11,75,000/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of the petition until realization.

5. Aggrieved by the said order, the present appeal has been preferred, contending that Sri Baburaya Bhagyashree And Ors vs Basappa Gurappa And Anr on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90251341/

sentences.text: Gundawan was an agriculturist and was also engaged in allied services, earning not less than Rs.15,000/- per month at the time of the accident in 2015.
However, the Tribunal considered his income as Rs.7,500/- per month, erred in awarding the compensation.

It is further contended that,
40% ought to have been added towards Future Prospects and that the amounts awarded under the conventional heads are on the lower side.
Accordingly, the appellants have sought to enhance the compensation and allow the appeal.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:5899 HC-KAR 6.
Though it is stated that the said Baburaya Gundawan was doing agriculture and earning Rs.15,000/-, there is no document is adduced to prove his income.

He met with an accident on 10.06.2015, as per the Karnataka Legal Services Authority, his income is to be taken as Rs.8,000/-
per month and the multiplier has to be taken as '18' and 40% towards Future Prospectus as per the citation reported in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi1 and 1/3rd is to be deducted towards personal expenses and Rs.40,000/- towards loss of Filial Consortium as per the citation reported in Magma General Insurance Co. Limited vs. Nanu Ram & Others2, as there are three dependents in the present appeal.

sentences.text:
Therefore, the claimants are entitled for the loss of dependency Rs.13,82,400/- (Rs.8,000 + 40% - 1/3rd x 12 x 18) and appellant No.1 is entitled for Rs.40,000/- for loss of spousal consortium and petitioner Nos.2 to 3 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of filial consortium i.e., Rs.1,20,000/-
(40,000 x 3).

The Tribunal has failed to award escalation of 10% on conventional heads for each three years (2017) 16 SCC 680 2018 ACJ 2782 NC: 2025:KHC-K:5899 HC-KAR from the date of accident, in terms of citation reported in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra).
7. In all, the total compensation comes to Rs.15,62,400/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

8. The award of compensation passed by the Tribunal is modified as under:
 Heads of compensation Amount  Loss of Dependency : Rs. 13,82,400/-
 (Rs.8,000 + 40% x 12 x 18 x  1/3rd)
 Loss of Estate : Rs. 15,000/-
 Loss of Funeral Expenses : Rs. 15,000/-
 Loss of spousal and filial : Rs. 1,20,000/-
 consortium (Rs.40,000 x 3)
 20% escalation for three : Rs. 30,000/-
 completed years of two terms on Bhagyashree And Ors vs Basappa Gurappa And Anr on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90251341/
3 conventional heads [Rs.1,20,000 + 15,000 + 15,000].
 TOTAL : Rs. 15,62,400/-

Accordingly, the claimants are entitle for total compensation of Rs.15,62,400/- as against Rs.11,75,000/-
NC: 2025:KHC-K:5899 HC-KAR awarded by the Tribunal and entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.3,87,400/-.
9.

In the result, the following order is passed:
 i) Appeal is allowed in part.

ii) The claimants are entitled for the total compensation of Rs.15,62,400/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
iii) The respondent No.2 - Insurance Company is directed to deposit the said amount with interest at 6% within a period of one month from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
iv) On such deposit, the claimants are permitted to withdraw the entire amount as per the apportionment of the Tribunal.

Sd/-
